items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: We had Eddie Atkins and Duterte. ... We had a good band.

ctx.x: Why did your brother play? Violin. What's his first name? Willie. Willie. Willie Foster. Yeah. I had Eddie Atkins. First we had Eddie Atkins.

We had Duterte for a while. We had Eddie Atkins and Duterte. King Oliver. Uh-huh. King Oliver. Uh-huh. Piku. Uh-huh. Had a guy called Chris. I never know what Chris's last name. Blaine Drum. Myself. Louis Kepp played guitar. We had a good band. Did you have some kind of a uniform? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
Yeah. And a guy with a uniform?

items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1958-08-24
items.q: John Robichaud, Papa Celeste, Eddie Atkins, another trumpet player. All them guys come from right up there around St. John's.

ctx.x: Yeah, I know Baby told me that you got him on the job.

I got Baby Dots, see. So we was getting around the end of the season we wanted another trumpet player. So Louie was playing with the O-Rey band down on Claiborne Street. Pete Laudas had a little dance hall. So I carried Johnny Strick was down there and enlisted Louie. He wanted Louie. And Louie come on the boat. So Louie moves music that he learned, he should give Joe Howard, the trumpet player, very good trumpet player. He's from up around St. John's, Louisiana. Him from St. John's, Louisiana. John Robichaud,…
